title: Zion’s safety depends on a pure people and a holy house
setting: Church members in Jackson County, Missouri, had formed a school of the prophets in the summer of 1833. Parley P. Pratt taught a class of about sixty men there each week. In early July, Oliver Cowdery and the school wrote to Joseph Smith in Kirtland, asking him to inquire about the school. Joseph dictated this revelation on 2 August and sent it to Missouri in a letter of 6 August. He did not yet know that a mob had attacked the Saints in Independence in late July.
summary: The revelation speaks to Joseph Smith about the Saints in Zion, many of whom are humble and seeking wisdom. It approves the school in Zion and Parley P. Pratt as its leader, as long as he abides in the Lord. Others in the school must be chastened, but the honest and contrite who keep their covenants by sacrifice are accepted. It then commands that a house be built in Zion, quickly, by the tithing of the people. The house is for thanksgiving and for instructing those called to the ministry. If it is kept undefiled, the Lord’s glory and presence will be there, and the pure in heart will see God. The revelation defines Zion as “the pure in heart.” Zion will escape coming judgments if she obeys, but will suffer if she does not.

contextNote.title: Zion defined by its people
contextNote.text: The Missouri Saints wanted guidance about their school and their future in Zion. Verse 21 answers by defining Zion as “the pure in heart,” not first as a piece of land. Verses 15–17 apply the same test to the planned house: the Lord’s glory will rest there only if it is not defiled. Verse 16 promises that “the pure in heart” who enter it “shall see God.” Verses 25–26 then make Zion’s safety conditional on obedience. In this passage, purity is the condition that turns a place into Zion.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson “For the Salvation of Zion” covers sections 94–97. It teaches that Zion is the pure in heart and that temples are places of instruction and of God’s presence. According to verses 13–16, what purposes does the Lord give for His house, and what does He ask of those who enter?
reviewNote: Read all 28 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 2 August 1833, in answer to a question about the school in Missouri, and notes the 23 July agreement to leave Jackson County. JSP historical introduction read for the two July letters, Pratt’s class of about sixty, the 6 August letter carrying three revelations, and Joseph’s unawareness of the July violence. JSP says the exact questions in the Missouri letters are unknown. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
